interactions.summary: Jiang dismisses judge-and-experiment theories of free will, shifts to a parent-child analogy, and lands on the idea that unconditional love reveals itself by allowing freedom.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with several student answers

claims.claim: A student suggests that because God is within human beings, human free will could be one way God experiences the material world from within creation.
Jiang rejects that line by insisting that God already has free will and pressing the class away from speculative complexity.
Another student proposes that free will lets God act more as judge, because actions taken from a true heart expose who people really are and can therefore be judged honestly.
Jiang says the class is overthinking the issue and reframes it through a child-parent analogy: unconditional love is recognized in the freedom a parent grants the child.
A student's follow-up at the end of the packet shows resistance to the shift, trying to return the discussion to law and judges just after Jiang declares free will the answer.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang collapses the theological puzzle into an intimate family signal: the clearest sign of love is the freedom you are given.
signature_moments.source_phrase: How do you know your parents truly love you unconditionally
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's decisive pedagogical turn from abstraction to lived intuition, and it becomes Jiang's main answer for why God gives free will.

signature_moments.moment: The judge model tries to make free will valuable because it reveals the person's true heart without camouflage.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It captures a rival account of freedom as disclosure rather than love, which Jiang is about to displace.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Used to name the interior motive that free action reveals and divine judgment could supposedly assess.
Jiang's answer for why free will exists: love proves itself by granting freedom rather than controlling behavior.
Named here as the direct analogue of parental freedom granted to a child and therefore as the sign of divine love.

chronology_notes.note: The packet continues the same June 15 classroom argument and introduces no cross-source chronology pressure.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student interjection at seg-0144 is grammatically broken in ASR but clearly functions as an attempted return to the earlier judge analogy.
